observation_summary: The system throws an IllegalFieldValueException when parsing '2 29' because it incorrectly validates the day against a non-leap year. The bug report and diff indicate that the year calculation logic in DateTimeFormatter.parseInto was flawed, using a time-zone-adjusted instant to determine the year instead of the base instant.
hypothesis: The bug is caused by an incorrect calculation of the 'defaultYear' in DateTimeFormatter.parseInto. The code currently uses the local time (instantLocal) to determine the year, which can shift the year incorrectly when the time zone offset is applied, especially near year boundaries. This incorrect year is then used to validate the date (e.g., Feb 29), causing an IllegalFieldValueException because the year is incorrectly identified as a non-leap year.
prediction: The fix involves changing the calculation of 'defaultYear' to use the original 'instantMillis' instead of 'instantLocal'.
experiment_rationale: The provided diff and bug report clearly show that the logic for determining the default year was flawed, leading to an incorrect year being used for validation. This is a procedural error in the calculation logic.
reasoning_summary: The bug is a classic case of incorrect algorithmic logic where the wrong variable (local time vs. UTC time) was used to derive a value (the year) used for subsequent validation. This fits the 'Algorithm/Method' category as it is a procedural error in the calculation of the default year.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the error manifests as a failed check (IllegalFieldValueException), the root cause is the incorrect calculation of the input value (the year) passed to the validation logic, not the validation logic itself.
